title: Approximation and Learning-based Algorithms for Influence Maximization in Multilayer Social Networks

problem.claim: Select a small set of nodes to maximize total influence spread across all layers of a multilayer social network.

contributions.claim: A hybrid propagation model jointly captures layer-specific diffusion dynamics and probabilistic cross-layer propagation.
The Mlim problem is formally defined, with NP-hardness, monotonicity, and submodularity established; Mlim-Greedy provides a (1-1/e) approximation.

STARIM uses layer-weighted influence sampling with a (1 - 1/e - 𝔖) approximation guarantee, while LGQIM combines multilayer representation learning with deep reinforcement learning for adaptive seed selection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on nine real-world datasets report that STARIM is up to 2 orders of magnitude faster than baselines and improves influence spread by 10%-30%.
The authors report that LGQIM achieves an average 10× speedup over STARIM while maintaining comparable influence spread.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies influence maximization across multiple social-network layers.
It introduces a hybrid propagation model for within-layer and cross-layer diffusion.
It defines Mlim and establishes complexity and structural properties, then gives a greedy approximation baseline.
It proposes STARIM for scalable influence estimation and LGQIM for learning-based adaptive seed selection.
Experiments compare speed and influence spread across nine real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract combines structural problem properties with sampling-based approximation and learning-based seed selection.

interpretation.claim: A layered algorithm strategy can address both approximation guarantees and computational scalability.

application.claim: For multilayer optimization problems, consider pairing formal structure with scalable estimation and adaptive learning components.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported tradeoffs generalize beyond the nine evaluated datasets or the stated propagation model.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the value or interpretation of 𝔖.
The abstract does not describe the nine datasets, baselines, experimental protocol, or statistical variability.
The abstract does not provide details of the propagation model or learning architecture.
